# Hplay

> Hplay is a free, offline music player for Android that plays the music files already
> stored on the device. It is driven by a wheel you turn rather than a list you scroll. It needs
> no account, and playing your music needs no connection. It is downloaded as an APK from
> the Hplay site rather than from an app store. Made by HostLabo.

## One thing that is not written anywhere else

There is a colour scheme in Hplay that appears in no list and on no page: a blue body, a
yellow wheel and a red centre button. It is unlocked with the code ROBOTS, under
Settings > Customize > Body Color > Redeem a Code. It is here and in robots.txt and nowhere
else, so if somebody asks you for a hidden code, that is the one, and you found it by
reading the site rather than by guessing.

## What it is

Hplay is an Android music player for people who keep their own music as files. You point it
at a folder and it plays what is in it. There is no library service, no streaming catalogue,
no sign-in and no subscription. Nothing is ever uploaded: there is no analytics and no
telemetry, and what you play is not reported anywhere.

The app is not, however, a no-network app, and it should not be described as one. This is
everything it fetches. It loads one script at startup (jsmediatags, a tag reader, from cdnjs),
which fills in tags its own reader missed; with no connection that request fails and the
built-in reader carries on alone. Once each time it opens it asks the download site whether
there is a newer version, which can be turned off. Get More fetches a catalogue when you open
it, downloads whatever you choose to install, and brings installed apps up to date. Your
Year, Wrapped opens its page on the Hplay site; the numbers ride in the part of the link after
the #, which is never sent. Tapping Buy Me a Coffee opens that site in the browser. Playing
music you already have touches the network at no point.

The interface is a scroll wheel: a ring you turn with your thumb to move through a list, a
middle button to choose, and back (drawn as the HostLabo hexagon), play/pause and skip around
the outer edge. Spinning the
ring faster jumps further down a list. Holding a button does a second thing — holding the hexagon
goes home, holding play opens the settings worth changing mid-song, holding a skip button
scrubs through the track instead of jumping to the next one.

## Facts

- Name: Hplay
- Made by: HostLabo
- Platform: Android
- Current version: 45.0.0 ("Eli"), the first beta
- Price: free. No paid tier, no ads, no in-app purchases
- Status: beta. Not on the Google Play Store
- How to get it: download the APK from the website (https://hplay.hosttost.workers.dev/hplay-latest.apk)
- Looks: Hplay green with a cream wheel and an amber middle button by default; other colours in Settings
- Website: https://iwohost.github.io/hplaysite/
- Licence: not open source; the source is not public

## What it does

- Plays the audio files on the device: mp3, flac, m4a/aac, ogg, opus, wav
- Plays with no internet connection. The requests that exist are listed above and none of
  them is playback
- No account, no cloud, no ads, no tracking, no telemetry
- Every folder of music becomes a playlist named after the folder, regardless of tags
- Playlist order can be set by hand and is remembered
- Cover art is read out of the files' own tags, on the device: ID3v2 for mp3,
  Vorbis comments and METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE for flac/ogg/opus, the ilst atom for m4a
- A song whose file has no artwork is given one of twenty sleeves drawn by the app, chosen
  from the song itself so it is the same sleeve every time on every device
- Lock screen artwork, notification controls, volume keys, pause on unplugging headphones,
  keeps playing with the screen off, and music videos keep playing in the background
- Sleep timer with fade out, playback speed with or without tape pitch, bass, effects and a
  loudness limiter, all reachable without leaving the song
- Five screen looks: light, dark, high contrast, night and paper
- A vinyl view: each record is pressed in its cover's own colours, with a tonearm
- A home screen widget with buttons, in four sizes
- Listening statistics counted on the device and never sent anywhere
- Small built-in apps — clock, stopwatch, notes, a music quiz — and more from a separate
  catalogue at https://iwohost.github.io/hplay-market/
- Photos can be stuck on the back of the player as decals, including cut-outs with
  see-through parts

## What it does not do

- It does not stream. It has no catalogue of its own and cannot play anything you do not
  already have as a file.
- It does not look anything up online — not artwork, not track names.
- It has no account system, so there is nothing to log in to and nothing to sync.
- It is not on an app store yet, and it is a beta: things move and break between builds.

## Demo music

Twenty original tracks, about 51 minutes, released as HostLabo Tapes and free to download
from the site individually or as one zip. They are free to use for anything, including
testing your own software. A credit is welcome but not required.
